title: Baptism of Jesus
summary: In the Gospel accounts, John baptised Jesus in the Jordan region; Luke ties John's ministry to the fifteenth year of Tiberius, which one scholar dates to AD 29, though others have proposed AD 26 to 28. John 1:28 names Bethany beyond the Jordan; Al-Maghtas in Jordan is the traditional site, though its veneration is Byzantine or later and a west-bank site is also claimed.

uncertainty.note: Luke 3:1 gives the fifteenth year of Tiberius; AD 29 on the usual count from Augustus's death in AD 14, AD 28 on inclusive counting, and AD 26-27 if counted from his co-rule.

as_recorded.value: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar's rule

where.modern_name: Al-Maghtas (Bethany Beyond the Jordan), Jordan, the traditional site; a rival site lies on the west bank
where.historical_name: Jordan valley; place named Bethany beyond the Jordan in John 1:28

importance.justification: The baptism opens Jesus's ministry in the Gospels and is a fixed point in attempts to date his life.

sources.title: Reckoning Tiberius's Reign and Jesus's Baptism
